question: Let \(f(x) = 100x^3 - 300x^2 + 200x.\) For how many real numbers \(a\) does the graph of \(y = f(x - a)\) pass through the point \((1, 25)?\)
solution:
Passing through \((1,25)\) means \(f(1-a)=25\). Set \(t=1-a\). Each real solution of \(f(t)=25\) gives exactly one value \(a=1-t\), so we can count where the original graph crosses the horizontal line \(y=25\).

Factor the polynomial:
\[
f(t)=100t(t-1)(t-2).
\]
Thus \(f(0)=f(1)=f(2)=0\), all below \(25\). Between the first two zeros,
\[
f\left(\frac12\right)
=100\left(\frac12\right)\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)
=37.5>25.
\]
Also,
\[
f(3)=100\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1=600>25.
\]
A polynomial is continuous, so its graph cannot move from below \(y=25\) to above it, or back, without crossing that line. Consequently there is a solution in each of
\[
\left(0,\frac12\right),\qquad
\left(\frac12,1\right),\qquad
(2,3).
\]
These intervals are disjoint, giving at least three distinct solutions. There cannot be more: \(f(t)-25\) is a cubic, and each distinct root contributes a linear factor, so it has at most three distinct roots.

There are therefore exactly \(\boxed{3}\) values of \(a\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
